While modern blockbusters depict these arena combatants as shredded, low-body-fat warriors with defined musculature, forensic analysis of their skeletons suggests a far more "insulated" reality. Their diet was so heavily reliant on carbohydrates like legumes and grain that they were colloquially known as "barley eaters," a regimen designed to create a layer of subcutaneous fat. This "padding" served a vital functional purpose, protecting internal organs from deep superficial slashes during public spectacles. What is the Latin nickname given to these fighters?
